albums.blurb: GoGo Penguin are a Manchester piano trio — Chris Illingworth on piano, Nick Blacka on double bass, Rob Turner on drums — who build their music from minimalist piano figures, propulsive bass lines, and drumming modeled on electronica breakbeats, all played acoustically. v2.0, released on Manchester's Gondwana Records in March 2014, is their second album, following 2012's Fanfares, and the record that broke them internationally, leading to a Blue Note deal two years later. The album is instrumental throughout.
albums.reception: v2.0 was shortlisted for the 2014 Mercury Prize, one of twelve albums nominated for the UK's album-of-the-year award.

albums.blurb: Fatimah Warner came up in Chicago's poetry-slam and open-mic scene alongside Chance the Rapper and Saba before releasing the mixtape Telefone in 2016. Room 25, self-released in September 2018, is her debut studio album, produced entirely by Phoelix with a live-band palette of soft keys, strings, and jazz chords under her conversational, spoken-word-inflected delivery. It chronicles the two years after Telefone, including her move from Chicago to Los Angeles, with guest turns from Ravyn Lenae, Smino, and Saba.
albums.reception: Pitchfork scored Room 25 an 8.6 and named it Best New Music, and Robert Christgau later ranked it the fifth-best album of the 2010s.

albums.blurb: Andy Shauf is a soft-spoken singer-songwriter from Regina, Saskatchewan who writes in character studies and plays nearly every instrument on his records himself, including the woodwind arrangements that have become his signature. The Party, released in May 2016 as his first album for ANTI-, is a concept record of interlocking vignettes that all take place over one night at the same house party, told through wry, closely observed portraits of its guests. It established the novelistic template he carried into The Neon Skyline and Norm.
albums.reception: The Party was shortlisted for the 2016 Polaris Music Prize, the ten-album final list for Canada's album-of-the-year award.
